source.section: Instructions PDF p.4, RI-1040 lines 1-5; PDF p.5, lines 6-8; PDF p.13, Tax Computation Worksheet ('Use for all filing status types')

worked: Federal AGI = wages 150,000.00 = 150,000.00. Federal taxable income = 150,000.00 - 31,500.00 standard deduction = 118,500.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). RI-1040 line 1 federal AGI 150,000.00. Line 1y total decreasing modifications = 0.00. Line 2a other-state obligations 0.00; line 2m total increasing modifications = 0.00. Schedule M page 2 line 3 net = 0.00 - 0.00 = 0.00; RI-1040 line 2 = 0.00. Line 3 modified federal AGI = 150,000.00 + (0.00) = 150,000.00. Standard Deduction and Exemption Worksheets: line 3 150,000.00 is not more than 254,250.00: the worksheets stop at line 3, full amounts. Line 4 standard deduction: 21,800.00 (Married filing jointly). Line 5 = 150,000.00 - 21,800.00 = 128,200.00. Line 6 exemptions: 2 x 5,100.00 = 10,200.00. Line 7 taxable income = 128,200.00 - 10,200.00 = 118,000.00. Line 8 tax on 118,000.00 by the schedule as numbers: 79,900.00 x 0.0375 = 2996.2500 + 38,100.00 x 0.0475 = 1809.750000 = 4,806.00. Credits 0.00 (Schedule I, Schedule II, RI earned income credit and RI-1040H are not modelled and not claimed here). Rhode Island income tax = 4,806.00. Note: Two exemptions on a joint return; line 3 well under 254,250.
